So when it was announced that Lee was allowing her manuscript to be published, Alabama Department of Human Resources looked into whether Lee was able to consent. I think her intense privacy and decades long refusal to publish anything added to the suspicion. Plus friends of hers say she is not quite as lucid as she once was, particularly after the stroke. However, Alabama recently dropped the investigation so it sounds like they didn't find anything. More than anything it's kinda weird that Harper Lee, arguably the most reclusive American author in history, suddenly wants to release a manuscript that she's apparently had for decades.In fact it essentially served as the "rough draft" version of Mockingbird. Only after her extremely protective sister dies and after Lee had a debilitating stroke. Full disclosure, I haven't read the book yet.

Pretty much what Roger_Mexico said; people have been suspecting "elder abuse" on the part of the publisher (and them taking advantage of a little old lady who doesn't know better).

Then again, if you're not privy to all their conversations and interactions first hand, it's kinda hard to tell if Lee is doing this because she's been "tricked" or just want to create a massive meal-ticket for her and her heirs ...

Either way @animem, the contrasting characterization of Atticus Finch is a good learning moment (both for creative writing and for literature students). It's how one character can be pictured / painted differently by the same author (Lee did write 'Go Set a Watchman' after all) and offers a meta-discussion on how people can be infinitely complex.

To that final point you made, my agent cited this book as the best example he's seen of the value in having a good editor. I haven't read the book and don't plan on it because of the main issues that have been raised, but what came out of it [Mockingbird] was an incredible book.
Seriously. I agree this book has real value as a look into the process and the craft of writing that as a reader I'm typically excluded from.

6 And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work. - Romans 11:6 (KJV)

 This verse is in Old English, but all it is saying is that you are either saved by grace, or saved by works, but not a combination of both. It is either you try and earn self-righteousness by doing the works of the law, or you accept the righteousness of God by grace, as a gift. If you try to earn your righteousness by working for it, then you are under the law, and if you do so, you will be judged by the law, and no one can be justified by the law (Romans 3:20). If you want to go to heaven, then you must put faith in the grace of God (Ephesians 2:8-9), and accept Jesus as your Lord and Savior (Romans 10:9-10).

 So many churches are still trying to teach the law, of telling you that you must tithe, attend church, witness, etc., for God to fellowship with you, or to get your prayers answered. This is making you earn self-righteousness under the law, and will not lead to heaven. You must put your faith entirely in Jesus, and not what you do, for you to be justified in the sight of God (Galatians 2:16). Jesus came to set us free from the curse of the law (Galatians 3:13), and He fulfilled the entire law for us (Matthew 5:17), so that we, by putting faith in what He did, can obtain His righteousness, and be totally justified in the sight of our Father. What a gift this is, to have our justification given to us, instead of having to work for it. Praise God for His plan of salvation, and praise Jesus for fulfilling it. Wow!
